text:
alex: Heads-up — reconciler surfaced ~9.8k orphaned token_usage events in the last 24h that didn't map to any attribution. I dumped a few examples to the S3 link: https://s3.aws/reports/orphaned-20260319 (cc @maria). Suspect fanout -> cold-path aggregator losing provenance pointer.

maria: Saw the dump, thanks. Quick question: are these all from eu-west-1 proxies or spread across regions?

chen: Quick check: ~73% eu-west-1, ~22% us-west-2, rest misc. This smells like the cold-path we added for burst traffic — we intentionally avoided attaching the full provenance to keep payloads small.

sam: If cold-path drops provenance, reconciler has no anchor to attribute tokens -> orphan. Two quick options: 1) rehydrate provenance in aggregator (bigger messages), or 2) attach a compact pointer (fingerprint/evidence id) that maps back to the full provenance later.

alex: I prefer option 2 to avoid inflating hotpath throughput. Proposal: add optional fields to the event envelope: `evidence_id`, `origin_shard`, and `origin_offset`. Reconciler can first try the direct attribution then fall back to a lookup by `evidence_id`. Example event we could emit from proxies:

```json
{
  "event_type": "token_usage",
  "token_id": "tok_8a7f...",
  "evidence_id": "e-8912b3c",
  "origin_shard": "proxy-eu-3",
  "origin_offset": "kafka://broker:9092/partition-12@345678",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-19T14:12:03Z"
}
```

maria: That looks good. Storage concern: adding `evidence_id` increases message size per event. Do we have numbers on ingest cost delta?

chen: Rough calc: `evidence_id` as 12-16 bytes base64 -> ~+30 bytes per event (with envelope overhead ~+50 bytes). At 1B tokens/day that’s ~50GB/day extra before compression. We can compress or make `evidence_id` a compact 64-bit fingerprint.

alex: Agreed — use 64-bit hex fingerprint (8 bytes) to keep cost low. Also make the field optional: old clients continue to work, new proxy hotpath writes it. Reconciler will treat missing `evidence_id` as before.

sam: Rollout plan suggestion (phased):
1) Add optional `evidence_id` + `origin_*` fields in schema (no client break).
2) Deploy proxies to emit fingerprint (canary 2 hosts).
3) Update reconciler to try direct attribution, then lookup by `evidence_id`. If found, attach attribution and emit audit marker.
4) Run a 72h backfill pass for windows where we saw spikes to validate mapping quality.
5) Switch reconciler to prefer `evidence_id` for cold-path events after 2w and enable stricter alerts.

chen: For the lookup backstore: we can keep a sharded KV that stores {evidence_id -> provenance}, TTL 7 days. Write path: proxies write to KV async (best-effort) and push event down pipeline. If KV miss, reconciler uses heuristic fingerprint match (tenant + short hash).

maria: Heuristic matches worry me for billing correctness. How often do we expect false positives? Can we attach a confidence score and only auto-apply at high confidence? Lower-confidence matches go to the manual audit queue.

alex: Yes — reconciler should emit `attribution_confidence` (high/medium/low). Only high => auto-apply. Medium/low => route to an audit/repair pipeline where we can run sampling and manual review.

billing-bot: :eyes: deploy-bot started canary emitting `evidence_id` on proxy-eu-3 (2 hosts) at 3912345685, status: healthy.

sam: Action items from this thread:
- chen: spike downselect and implement compact 64-bit fingerprint writer (ETA 2d).
- alex: update reconciler to accept fallback evidence lookup + confidence scoring (ETA 3d).
- maria: estimate cost+retention for 7-day KV and sampling storage (ETA EOD).
- ops: canary proxies and monitor ingestion size and reconciler false-neg rate.

alex: If we get the confidence scoring + optional compact id in, this should eliminate most orphaned cases without blowing up ingest. Thanks all — follow up in the check-in tomorrow.
